## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

Cube gone. Every surface now carries `d2m`.

**What changed**

- **`app/icon.svg`** — favicon is now `d2m` in Geist SemiBold, reduced to outlines (a favicon has no webfont to set text in). Keeps the light/dark `prefers-color-scheme` switch.
- **`app/apple-icon.tsx`** — white `d2m` on the dark plate. Verified the rendered 180×180 PNG.
- **`app/og/route.tsx`** — share card header is now `d2m  Dhruv Sharma`. Verified the rendered 1200×630.
- **`lib/mark.ts`** — `cubeSvg`/`cubeDataUri` → `markSvg`/`markDataUri`, plus `MARK_VIEW_BOX`/`MARK_RATIO` so a wordmark gets sized by its own ratio instead of stuffed in a square.
- **`components/site-mark.tsx` → `site-figure.tsx`** — the `SiteMark` cube export was already dead (nothing imported it), so it's deleted. The hero drawing survives as `SiteFigure`, renamed because "site-mark" pointing at something that isn't the mark is the exact confusion you're clearing out.
- **`lib/mark.test.ts`** — new. The favicon is a static file and can't import the outline, so a test asserts its path data matches `MARK_PATH` byte for byte.

Outlines were extracted from the repo's own `Geist-SemiBold.ttf` at `-0.025em` tracking, so it's the same letterforms as `ShortMark`, not a lookalike. Semibold rather than the panel's medium — at raster sizes the extra weight is what survives.

`grep -i cube` is clean, typecheck passes, lint clean, 126 tests pass, build succeeds.

**One caveat on legibility:** at 32px and up the favicon reads clearly. At 16px it's mush — inherent to any three-letter wordmark at that size, and unavoidable while the mark stays `d2m`. Most browsers pull 32px+ on retina, so this mostly won't bite.

- `components/icons.tsx` — `MapPinIcon` and `ClockIcon` had no other callers
- `lib/site.ts` — `location` and `timezone` fields, now unreferenced
- `DESIGN.md` §3 described the panel as holding location and local time; updated

`AI_ACTIVITY_TIMEZONE` in `lib/ai-activity-payload.ts` is a separate constant driving the activity grid — left alone.

Verified against the built server: `New Delhi`, `Asia/Kolkata`, the `--:-- --` placeholder and the maps link are all absent from the rendered homepage. The panel keeps its own top/bottom hairlines — the `screen-line-bottom` I removed was the internal divider between the facts and the socials, and there's nothing left to divide.
